To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TiO2/ITO modified electrodes were developed for the quantitative photooxidation of adsorbed dsDNA, which can be used as a model to study the effect and the mechanisms of the antioxidants as dsDNA protecting agents.
the TiO2/MB/DNA modified ITO electrode is able to detect the presence of ROS and that it can be used to quantify the protective action of different antioxidant compounds.
the developed TiO2/MB/DNA sensor is able to detect the presence of ROS and the antioxidant properties of the tested substances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of electrochemical DNA sensors based on TiO2 modified electrodes.
the development of new electrochemical DNA biosensors based on TiO2 modified electrodes.
the development of new electrochemical DNA-based sensors, and the application of these sensors to the study of the antioxidant properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TiO2/ ITO electrodes are able to oxidize ds-DNA through ROS and that the ds-DNA oxidation is prevented by the addition of antioxidants.
the TiO2/MB sensor has been successfully applied to the evaluation and monitoring of the antioxidant properties and the protective effect of glutathione, gallic acid, and ascorbic acid.
the electrochemical method described here is a very sensitive, simple, and rapid method for the detection of ds-DNA oxidation and for the study of antioxidant activity of small molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developed ds-DNA modified electrodes have been applied for the first time to the quantitative evaluation of the antioxidant activity of glutathione (GSH) and gallic acid (GA) in the presence of ds-DNA as a model of biological target.
we developed an electrochemical sensor to evaluate antioxidant properties of compounds by studying their ability to protect DNA from oxidative damage.
we were able to develop and apply an efficient electrochemical method to monitor the effect of different antioxidants on the stability of DNA in the presence of ROS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrochemical sensor can be used to study the effect that antioxidants have on DNA structure, and it is possible to use the sensor for the evaluation of the efficiency of the antioxidants as protecting agents of ds-DNA.
the electrochemical detection of ds-DNA oxidation products is a powerful tool to evaluate the antioxidant activity of different compounds.
the electrochemical sensor can be successfully used to evaluate the antioxidant properties of a wide range of antioxidants.
